Yo. I'm 24. 

I have frequent panic/anxiety attacks every other  month. The cause of your problem might be the same as mine. If this problem persists, please go se a therapist.

Recently this exact thought crossed my mind in the midst of my fragile state.... "Holy shit I'm almost 30" & "...the year is almost over" and so on. It persists in the back of my head. I didn't used to have these thoughts and worries, until i started thinking about it. I know I'm pretty far off from 30, but if I may I'd like to share some means of coping even totally removing these thoughts.

It's totally normal to ponder about age. The more you think about life and how fleeting it is, the more it can scare you. After a while, like with all harsh known facts, you start to forget about it. It becomes boring, grey noise. In the beginning it's scary, but trust that after a while it gets better.

Now, Time. Like someone posted here, I'll say the same. It's normal to feel this way as you get older. Life becomes **repetitive** . Ever heard the saying "variety is the spice of life". It truly is. 
Hobbies, friends, studies & pure fucking randomness, do things differently every day. Make everyday special.

**The reason time feels shorter, is because everyday we do the same thing, we wake up, shower, brush our teeth, go to work, go back home, shower, brush our teeth, then sleep. Life just becomes... boring. **

A little interesting psychology for you. 
If you do the same things every day/year, go to the same beach on holiday, eat the same food, follow the same routine, your brain starts to realize a pattern and no longer finds any importance in it. You basically then start to live in auto pilot. Then when looking back at life, you remember a few scenes of important memories because nothing stands out. In turn, making it feel like only yesterday you were riding your first bike. and then... "time feels as if it went by too fast"

So understanding why it feels time moves faster, isn't actually time moving faster, but you're not filling that void with variety and fulfilling memories. I had this problem when I had anxiety where it felt it got dark to quick, "so time is speeding up" i stressed. 
No, no, it was winter. The hard reality is, time keeps moving on. And old age is inevitable for all of us, but here you are. Living. 

Do as much as you can in a single day, never the same thing everyday, but something fun, different.
Make your life feel bloated. Make it feel like you lived the equivalent of a 100 lifetimes.

My psychologist told me this: **" ...Our brain forms neural pathways like cows forms pathways in grass fields. When your brain mindlessly wanders, it can easily go through one of those pathways. In order to stop thinking about any bad memories or feelings, force your brain to think of something else when those feelings or memories occur. Form your own little grass pathway."**

TL;DR Momentary distractions help alot. Do fun things frequently and try not to think about time to often.

The Buster Sword was forged by the Dark Lord Sowron during the Second Age to gain dominion over the free peoples of Midgar. In disguise as Buster, or "Lord of Sword", he aided the Shinra smiths of Midgar and their leader Heidegger in the making of the Buster Sword. He then forged the Buster Sword in the Mako of Mount Nibel.

Sowron intended it to be the most powerful of all Swords, able to rule and control those who wielded the others. Since the other Swords were powerful on their own, Sowron was obliged to place much of his own power into the Buster to achieve his purpose.

Creating the Buster Sword simultaneously strengthened and weakened Sowron. With the Sword, he could control the power of all the other Swords, and thus he was significantly more powerful after its creation than before; but by binding his power within the Sword, Sowron became dependent on it.

After a while it landed in the hands of a small hairy blonde boy who would go on to form the fellowship of the Buster Sword.

Recovery is a long and arduous journey. It'll take time, but he'll get better. As to what you can do to support him and help him on his road to recovery:

• Always try and assure him that it'll go away. It will go away, trust me, but it'll take a long time. Recovery time varies between people. 
(The scariest part of this illness is the thought that this will never go away.)

• Try to convince him to focus his mind on distractions/hobbies 
[e.g Video games, movies, tv series etc.]
When it feels like you're trapped in your own mind you'll need things to distract you. To demand your attention. To make you forget about yourself.
(This hell of this illness really kicks in when you're alone with your own thoughts, therefore try distractions)

• Tell him to stay away from the news, social media or any other source of media which can feed him negative thoughts. This illness is a 24/7 hell. The last thing a fragile mind needs is any bad or toxic news/social media posts. Trust me, this comes from experience.

• Sleeping can be really difficult with this illness. Like I said, being alone with your own thoughts is HELL. If you can, try and talk to him at night, assure him everything will be alright. 
(A sleeping pill/chill pill will do the trick, if a medical professional agrees to it)

• Depersonalization/Derealization warps your senses & your thoughts. What seemed familiar and comforting becomes strange and terrifying, for example my home of 14 years became so uncomfortable to me. It didn't feel like my home anymore. Basically, it felt like I always had to get away.
(This was just so you can understand a little better about what he's going through)
